text:
nora: quick heads-up — two OOMs on rtx3 during long-convo load test (seqs ~12k tokens). KV cache went from 3.2GB -> 12.1GB over ~10m, paging started at 9.6GB then OOM at 12.1GB.

sam: ugh. can you paste the heap summary + timeline? which kernel was active?

nora: here's the gist:
```
2026-03-18T12:01:22Z kv_total=3.2GB kv_frag_ratio=0.42 active_slots=98k reuse_hits=0.12
2026-03-18T12:06:10Z kv_total=9.8GB kv_frag_ratio=0.61 active_slots=112k reuse_hits=0.05 paging=started
2026-03-18T12:11:30Z OOM: alloc failed for kv slab (requested 48MB)
```
kernel: quant-opt-v2 (auto-picked), batching=continuous, slot_alloc_strategy=sticky

tom: looks like fragmentation + sticky reuse is producing many small slabs. frag ratio jumped to 0.61. can we repro with the long-context harness? link: https://dash/repro/2999

raj: two quick asks: 1) what's `slot_reclaim_threshold` now? 2) do we have `kv_compact` running?

nora: threshold=0.7, compact_every=off (we disabled it in nov rollout for perf). repro command:
```
./tools/load_test --model redwood-1 --seq-length 12000 --concurrency 4 --repro-kv
```

eva: proposal: re-enable background compaction with conservative knobs and add a fast fallback: if kv_used_ratio > 0.9 then 1) start compact, 2) stop accepting new long sessions (reject >8k tokens), 3) switch to ephemeral quantized kernel for those sessions. small patch + feature flag.

sam: +1. we should also add alert `kv_fragment_ratio > 0.55 for 5m` so SRE warns earlier.

tom: another mitigation we tried offline: evict by reuse_score (least recently reused prefixes first) instead of oldest-first; that kept working set smaller in sim. we can try an A/B rollout.

infra-bot: deploy started for canary=5% patch=nora/kv-compact-flag #PR 5123

nora: I'll add the compact_every=30s flag and injectable evict_policy param. leaving a TODO to collect `kv_fragment_ratio` and per-slot sizes in telemetry.

eva: i'll own the canary watch. if tail latency spikes >10% or OOMs recur roll back.

raj: after canary, plan: 24h soak, then ramp to 50% if metrics look ok. file an incident playbook update with steps for manual flush.

sam: for postmortem collect: heap dumps, per-slot histograms, and kernel selection logs (`/var/log/kernel-switch.log`).

nora: ack. adding logs + reproducer to the ticket. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
